direction_notes: Bone-conducted 40 kHz ultrasound activated the medial portion of the primary auditory cortex (BA41) in both normal-hearing and profoundly deaf subjects, though the increase in rCBF was significantly smaller in the deaf group.

exposures.label: Bone-conducted 40 kHz ultrasound (AM by 1 kHz tone bursts) via ultrasonic hearing aid

target.label: medial portion of the left transverse temporal convolutions (Brodmann's area 41)

timing.protocol_description: A 40 kHz sinusoid was amplitude-modulated by 1 kHz tone bursts (100 ms length, 10 ms linear rise/fall ramps, 600 ms inter-burst interval) and presented on the right sternocleidomastoid muscle via an ultrasound vibrator while subjects lay supine with eyes closed/patched; each subject underwent 10 consecutive PET scans (rest and hearing-aid conditions).

source_quotes.n_subjects: Subjects: We studied nine normal volunteers, all men, aged 22-49 years (mean 30.6 years), who were all righthanded according to the Edinburgh inventory [9]. They had no history of hearing deficits. The protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board, and all subjects gave their written informed consent for the study.
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: Stimulus presentation: Tone bursts of 1 kHz with a length of 100 ms, including linear 10 ms rising and falling ramps, were presented through the hearing aids. The inter-burst interval was set at 600 ms. For the ultrasonic hearing aid a 40 kHz sinusoid, amplitude-modulated by the 1 kHz tone bursts, was presented on the right sternoclaid mastoid muscle using a ultrasound vibrator (MA40E7S, Murata Co. Kanazawa, Ishikawa, Japan). For the vibro-tactile hearing aid the tone bursts were presented as the most clearly perceiving tactile sensation level using a tactile hearing aid (TACTAID 7, Audiological Engineering Corp. Somerville, MA, USA). Among the seven vibrators of TACTAID 7, only one vibrator giving the highest sensitivity for the tone bursts was attached 2 cm below the ultrasound vibrator. For the air-conducted sonic hearing aid the tone bursts were presented through ear-insertion type stereo headphones (EarTone, EARCabot Safty Corp., Indianapolis, USA) at the most clearly perceiving (MCP) level determined for each subject, which was a sensation level of 60 dB on average. For the bone-conducted sonic hearing aid a bone conduction stimulator (Audiometer AA67, Rion Co., Kokubunji, Tokyo, Japan) was attached at the forehead and the bursts were presented at the MCP level.

source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: A complete session consisted of two rest scans and eight scans with hearing conditions through four different types of hearing aid: bone-conducted ultrasonic (U), vibro-tactile (V), airconducted sonic (A), and bone-conducted sonic (B) hearing aids.

flags.reason: paper states two separate group sizes (9 normal-hearing, 5 profoundly deaf) but never a single combined total exposed to the ultrasonic device; recorded as a list.

normal subjects received an unstated number of ultrasound (U) scans within 8 hearing-aid scans across 4 device types; deaf subjects explicitly received 5 ultrasound scans; the two groups differ and no single number is stated for the normal group, so left not_reported.
paper states a 600 ms inter-burst interval but not whether this is the full period between burst onsets or only the silent gap between bursts, so PRF was not computed.
profound deafness is not in the conditions vocabulary; recorded via other/condition_other.
